clue.text: It was in Christ's nature to be poorly shod amid the suffering

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the reworked letters sit inside the word for suffering

parts.note: gip (also spelt gyp) is pain or suffering, as in 'my knee is giving me gip'

indicators.note: poorly signals the letters of shod are in a bad way and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that Christ, poorly shod, walked among the suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: GIP is a variant spelling of gyp, a British colloquial word for pain, as in 'my back is giving me gyp'.
explanation.definitionFit: Divine status or deity is what the clue describes as part of Christ's nature in Christian doctrine.

clue.text: Sea beast's to dine and spread upward

indicators.note: in a down clue, upward means the combined letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to sup is to dine, especially on an evening meal
marg is short for margarine, a spread for bread

explanation.surface: A sea creature's routine is to eat and then spread upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Sea beast' is a link, read as 'is'; 'upward' turns the whole run because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The grampus is Risso's dolphin, or loosely a killer whale, a large marine mammal.

clue.text: Successful dog's home in spring

indicators.note: dog's read as dog has, so the dog holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: taken as written
in means at home, as in 'staying in tonight'
a well is a spring of water from the ground

explanation.surface: A dog's kennel set beside a spring, apparently a sign of prosperity.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'dog's' stands for 'has', putting IN (at home) inside DOG to give DOING; 'in' is then just a link before WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thriving or prospering is said to be getting on well in life, which matches being successful.

clue.text: Audibly intoxicated female, a great laugher

indicators.note: audibly means the words are to be heard spoken rather than read as spelt

parts.note: high means intoxicated, a hen is a female bird, then a as written

explanation.surface: A tipsy woman who is loud and laughs a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, HIGH HEN A runs together into the name of the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena is famous for its cackling call, often likened to laughter.

clue.text: Gave coat to drunk

definitions.meaning: covered a wall or ceiling with a layer of lime or gypsum paste

explanation.surface: Someone painted a wall, or got very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To apply plaster gives a wall a coat; plastered is also slang for heavily intoxicated.

clue.text: Thus honour deceased invalid's support

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed
KBE, Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
d is a standard abbreviation for died or deceased

explanation.surface: A dead knight's honours displayed beside an invalid's bed.
explanation.walkthrough: KBE is a British knighthood award.
explanation.definitionFit: A sick person is supported by the bed they lie in while ill.

clue.text: Stop to eat a dish

indicators.note: to eat means the first word takes the next one inside it

parts.note: to stay is to stop or remain somewhere

explanation.surface: Pausing for a bite of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts A inside STAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Satay is a Southeast Asian food of skewered grilled meat with peanut sauce.

clue.text: What keeps the House united — unoriginal bomb scares, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters given could be arranged another way
unoriginal means bomb loses its original, its first letter

explanation.surface: Copycat bomb hoaxes threatening the unity of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unoriginal' strips the B from bomb, leaving OMB; 'perhaps' rearranges OMB + SCARES. A cross-beam literally holds a house's structure together.
explanation.definitionFit: A structural transverse beam ties the walls of a building together, keeping the house in one piece.

clue.text: Destined for the jump

explanation.surface: Headed for the leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Bound means certain or headed for something; it is also a leap or spring forward.

clue.text: Excuses for the respect the Queen's lost

definitions.note: plural in the clue, but defence works as a mass noun covering justifying excuses

indicators.note: lost means a piece goes missing from the word for respect

parts.note: deference is polite respect
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: Justifications for a show of respect that the monarch has abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes ER out of DEFERENCE. ER is the cipher of Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A defence is a justification or plea offered to excuse an action.

clue.text: Stand for one in the rear

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the word for the rear

parts.note: arse is British slang for backside
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A substitute player waiting in the background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside ARSE, British slang for the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To arise is to get up or stand up from sitting or lying.

clue.text: Artificial surface provides a lively ride in the foam

indicators.note: in means one piece sits within the word for the foam

parts.note: surf is the foam of breaking waves
a trot is a brisk gait on horseback

explanation.surface: A riding display on a fake pitch, splashing through the spray.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a horse ride through sea spray; the definition is the synthetic grass brand.
explanation.definitionFit: AstroTurf is a brand of synthetic grass used on sports pitches.

clue.text: Time in the storeroom for "Pomp and Circumstance"

indicators.note: in means the time word goes inside the word for the storeroom

parts.note: a pantry is a small storeroom for food
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Elgar's march played for ages in the larder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pomp and Circumstance' is a set of Elgar marches, but the phrase means ceremonial display.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremonial splendour and spectacle is what the phrase pomp and circumstance describes.

clue.text: Irishman keeping driver's head on passenger seat?

indicators.note: keeping means the name holds a letter within it

parts.note: Sean is a common Irish man's name

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An Irish chap in a car holding the driver's head beside the passenger seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes D from driver's; 'keeping' puts it inside SEAN. The surface suggests a car, but the seat is a sedan chair carried by bearers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair is an enclosed seat carried on poles, conveying a single passenger.

clue.text: Overdoes things in dubious establishment

definitions.meaning: cooks for too long, or gets worked up over things
an old word for a brothel

explanation.surface: Someone over-indulging in a disreputable house.
explanation.definitionFit: Stews means simmers too long or frets; historically the stews was a brothel district.

clue.text: Biblical hero and biblical villain about to spoil one

indicators.note: about means the villain's name goes around the other pieces

parts.note: Satan is the chief adversary in the Bible
to mar is to spoil or damage
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Bible story pairing a good man and an evil one, poised to ruin someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The Good Samaritan is the hero of Jesus's parable in Luke's Gospel; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Good Samaritan in Luke's Gospel is the heroic figure who helps the robbed traveller.

clue.text: Affectedly erudite singer appearing in unopened nursery

indicators.note: appearing in means the singer is placed inside the other word
unopened means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a creche is a day nursery for small children
Cher is a famous American singer

explanation.surface: A pretentious pop star turning up at a nursery that has not yet opened.
explanation.walkthrough: A creche is a nursery; 'unopened' tells you to drop its first letter before the singer goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Recherché means rare, exotic or precious, carrying a sense of over-refinement and studied obscurity.

clue.text: Shellfish rewriting the bloody ABC

indicators.note: rewriting means the letters that follow are written out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A frustrated pupil copying out the wretched alphabet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewriting' rearranges BLOODY ABC. A clabbydoo is a Scottish word for a large mussel.
explanation.definitionFit: A clabbydoo, a Scots dialect term, is a large mussel or similar bivalve mollusc.

clue.text: Complained one has space for hedonistic philosophy

parts.note: carped means found fault or complained
I is the Roman numeral for one
an em is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: A grumbler making room for a pleasure-seeking outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: An em is a typographic space the width of a letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpe diem, Latin for seize the day, is a motto urging enjoyment of the present.

clue.text: The disorder a child may wreak!

definitions.text: The disorder a child may wreak!

indicators.note: disorder means the letters of the next words are thrown into confusion

explanation.surface: A warning about the chaos a toddler can cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' rearranges A CHILD MAY. The whole clue also defines: the infection is a disorder that a child could, sadly, pass on.
explanation.definitionFit: Chlamydia is a sexually transmitted bacterial infection, a medical condition or disorder.

clue.text: Small volume about girl compiler is a great work

indicators.note: about means the measure goes around the other pieces

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetre, is a small unit of volume
lass is a girl
I, the setter or compiler, referring to themselves

explanation.surface: A slim book about a girl, written by its compiler, hailed as a masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves 'compiler', 'setter' or 'me', all giving I.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is a work of art or literature of lasting excellence.

clue.text: Instrument returned to married woman

indicators.note: returned means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: a lyre is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A harp given back to a wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'woman' defines: Meryl is a given name, as with the actress Meryl Streep.
explanation.definitionFit: Meryl is a woman's given name, as in the actress Meryl Streep.

clue.text: Council, conversely, was behind schedule?

indicators.note: conversely means the two parts of the phrase are taken the other way round

parts.note: ran late means was behind schedule

explanation.surface: A committee meeting that overran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversely' swaps the two words of RAN LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lateran Councils were five ecumenical church councils held in Rome's Lateran Palace.

clue.text: Companion leaves the room with preserving agent

indicators.note: leaves means a piece departs from the word for the room

parts.note: a chamber is a room
CH, Companion of Honour, is a British order

explanation.surface: A friend walks out of the room carrying a preservative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes CH out of CHAMBER. Fossil resin keeps insects intact, hence a preserving agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Fossil tree resin famously preserves insects trapped in it for millions of years.

clue.text: Argument for grill

explanation.surface: A dispute over a barbecue.
explanation.definitionFit: Broil is an old word for a noisy quarrel, and in American usage means to cook under direct heat.

clue.text: Where to get drink, drug and perfume when beginning to grow up

parts.note: a pub is where drinks are served
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
scent is perfume

explanation.surface: A teenager's first nights out: pub, pills and aftershave.
explanation.definitionFit: A pubescent person is reaching puberty, at the stage of adolescence.

clue.text: Looks and sounds like a diarist

indicators.note: sounds like signals that the word is to be heard spoken, not read as spelt

parts.note: Samuel Pepys was the famous 17th-century English diarist, his name said with a long e

explanation.surface: A glance that resembles a famous journal writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Pepys kept a famous diary of 1660s London.
explanation.definitionFit: Peeps are quick glances, so the word means looks as a noun or verb.

clue.text: Sedate singularly famous cricketer

indicators.note: singularly means the name is made singular by dropping its plural-looking final letter

parts.note: Sir Garfield Sobers was a great West Indian all-rounder

explanation.surface: A calm, uniquely celebrated player.
explanation.walkthrough: Garry Sobers, a West Indian cricketer, loses his S as if it were a plural ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Sober means serious, calm and staid, a close synonym of sedate.

clue.text: Swimmer taking the gold (first) by a narrow margin

indicators.note: taking means the fish holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a shad is a fish, so a swimmer

indicators.note: first means gold comes before the word next to it

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A swimmer narrowly winning gold.
explanation.walkthrough: '(first)' fixes the order of gold and 'the'. In horse racing a short head is the smallest winning distance.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing, winning by a short head is winning by the slimmest margin.

clue.text: Cheese recipe — smoked? It may be

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
R is an abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, take

explanation.surface: A recipe for smoked cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the heather root carved into tobacco pipes, so the thing that may be smoked; 'smoked' tempts you to think of cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Briar root is the wood from which tobacco pipes are made, so a pipe of it is smoked.

clue.text: The first of the state boundaries

parts.note: Cal is short for California, a US state
ends are boundaries or limits

explanation.surface: Something at the very edge of a state's borders.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Roman calendar the calends were the first day of each month.
explanation.definitionFit: The calends was the opening day of a Roman month.

clue.text: The blade-wielder in classical art in the sultanate

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the name of the sultanate

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian Peninsula
ars is Latin, the classical language, for art

explanation.surface: A swordsman depicted in Arabian classical art.
explanation.walkthrough: The blade is an oar's flat end, not a sword; Latin is the classical language, hence 'classical art'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower handles an oar, whose flat end is called the blade.
